newsitem.title: UK: NWE gas oil slips on stocks data, diesel tight.
newsitem.headline: NWE gas oil slips on stocks data, diesel tight.

text.p: NWE heating oil eased after U.S. data showed an unexpected build in stocks last week, but diesel demand remained very strong, traders said.

Premiums for heating oil cargoes were steady, with a cargo sold into Hamburg at Nov IPE +$11 cif, but Nov IPE futures fell $1.75 to $238.75 per tonne. Oct IPE, which expires on Thursday, fell $1.00 to $245.50 per tonne.

Premiums on the heating oil barge market slipped $1.00 to talk around Oct IPE +$5 for prompt delivery and traders saw increasing supplies from the U.S. and Russia. Second-half Oct barges were steady at Oct IPE +$1.00. U.S. distillate stocks rose 1.3 million barrels last week, but were still 15 percent below last year, according to the Energy Information Administration.
While heating oil barge premiums slipped, diesel premiums climbed further on very limited supply and strong demand in France and Germany.
One late-Oct cargo offer at Nov IPE +$30 cif NWE was considering retreating towards +$33 as the buyers stepped up their bids.
Algerian cargoes were valued above $30 cif NWE, and diesel barges traded up to Oct +$24/25 fob ARA for prompt delivery.
